claim: Every K4-free graph is the union of countably many triangle-free graphs; equivalently no K4-free graph has triangle cover number above aleph-null, which would answer Erdos problem 595 negatively.

facets.entities: K4-free graphs, finite and infinite, and their triangle-free edge decompositions
facets.mechanism: countable decomposition of a clique-free graph into subgraphs omitting a smaller clique, the Erdos-Hajnal countable escape phenomenon
facets.method: Folkman and Nesetril-Rodl finite arrowing constructions, compactness, chromatic dispersion, uncountable chromatic number structure theorems
facets.outcome: existence or nonexistence of an infinite K4-free graph that is not a countable union of triangle-free graphs
